Predict an Observed Clinical Effect from Two Observed Surrogate Effects

Source: R/clinical_predictive_distribution.R
clinical_predictive_distribution.Rd

Generates equally weighted predictive draws for a new trial's observed clinical treatment-effect estimate using historical posterior and observed treatment effects on the surrogate endpoints.

Usage

clinical_predictive_distribution(
  mcmc_dat,
  sample_dat,
  seed = NULL,
  diffuse = FALSE,
  diffuse_se = 100,
  intercept0 = FALSE
)

Arguments

mcmc_dat

Historical posterior draws as posterior_samples returned by historical_model_fit_2surrogates() function.

sample_dat

A named list containing ClnSE, Sur1Est, Sur1SE, Sur2Est, Sur2SE, R1Clin, R2Clin, and R12 for the one trial for which we wish to estimate the posterior predictive distribution.

seed

Optional positive integer for reproducible simulation. When supplied, the caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

diffuse

Logical; replace the historical surrogate-effect distribution with a diffuse prior, as in surrogate_MBE(). Defaults to FALSE (full carryover).

diffuse_se

Positive standard deviation of the diffuse surrogate prior.

intercept0

Logical; center the clinical-intercept draws at zero, as in surrogate_MBE(). Defaults to FALSE. An absent clinical-intercept column in a fixed-intercept fit is treated as zero.

Value

A numeric vector of posterior predictive distribution of the treatment effect on the clinical endpoint. The length is same as the number of rows of the historical posteriors.

Details

Review the details provided in surrogate_MBE(). We can use the historical posterior draws and the observed treatment effect on the surrogate effects to sample posterior distribution on the true treatment effect on the clinical endpoint. Note also $$\hat{\theta}_0 \sim N(\theta_0, \sigma^2_0)$$ where \(\sigma^2_0\) is the known sampling variance of the clinical treatment effect (i.e., ClnSE of the new trial). We can then collect the predictive distribution on the observed clinical treatment effect by sampling the error term from \(N(0, \sigma^2_0)\) and adding it to the surrogate MBE's posterior distribution of the true clinical effect.

Examples

data("historical_posterior")
data("trial_sim_dat")
held_out <- list(
  ClnSE = trial_sim_dat$CE_se[1],
  Sur1Est = trial_sim_dat$Sur1_est[1],
  Sur1SE = trial_sim_dat$Sur1_se[1],
  Sur2Est = trial_sim_dat$Sur2_est[1],
  Sur2SE = trial_sim_dat$Sur2_se[1],
  R1Clin = trial_sim_dat$Cor_CE_Sur1[1],
  R2Clin = trial_sim_dat$Cor_CE_Sur2[1],
  R12 = trial_sim_dat$Cor_Sur1_Sur2[1]
)
predictive <- clinical_predictive_distribution(
  mcmc_dat=historical_posterior,
  sample_dat=held_out,
  seed = 2026
)
stats::quantile(predictive, c(0.025, 0.975))
#>       2.5%      97.5% 
#> -0.4234108  0.2733332
